drafts.walkScript: Empty seats are 8,006 minus 3,478. The tens and hundreds hold 0, so exchange from the thousands. The ones become 16, the tens and hundreds become 9, and the thousands 7. 16 minus 8 is 8, 9 minus 7 is 2, 9 minus 4 is 5. 7 minus 3 is 4, so 4528 seats were empty.

Perimeter is the distance all the way round the rectangle. It has two sides of 8 cm and two sides of 3 cm. One long and one short side make 8 plus 3, which is 11 cm. Double 11 cm to get 22 cm. 24 cm comes from 8 times 3, which finds the area instead.
Write £5 as £5.00 so the pounds and pence line up with £3.50. Take £3 from £5.00 to leave £2.00. Then take the 50p to leave £1.50. So Sam gets £1.50 change.

Write 582 above 147, lining up hundreds, tens and ones. In the ones, 2 is on top and smaller than 7, so exchange a ten. 12 minus 7 is 5, and the tens now hold 7. 7 minus 4 is 3, and 5 minus 1 is 4, giving 435. 445 takes 2 from 7 in the ones instead of exchanging.

Divide 4,872 by 4 one digit at a time, from the left. 4 divided by 4 is 1, and 8 divided by 4 is 2. 7 divided by 4 is 1, with 3 left over. Carry the 3 to make 32, and 32 divided by 4 is 8, giving 1218. 1210 comes from dropping the 3 left over.

Add 3,458 and 2,673 column by column, starting with the ones. 8 plus 3 is 11, so write 1 and carry 1. 5 plus 7 plus 1 is 13, so write 3 and carry 1. 4 plus 6 plus 1 is 11, so write 1 and carry 1. 3 plus 2 plus 1 is 6, giving 6131.

Start with the eggs bought: 12 trays of 30 is 360 eggs. Take away the 48 that break, leaving 312 eggs. 312 shared into boxes of 6 is 52 boxes. 60 forgets the broken eggs, and 68 adds the 48 instead. 312 stops before packing the boxes.

Give both fractions the same bottom number, 45. 2/5 is the same as 18/45, and 2/9 is the same as 10/45. 18/45 is more than 10/45, so 2/5 is bigger. 2/9 has the bigger bottom number, but that cuts the whole into smaller parts.
40% means 40 out of 100, which is two fifths. One fifth of 60 is 60 divided by 5, which is 12. Two fifths is 12 times 2, which is 24. 6 is only 10% of 60, and 20 is 60 take away 40.

Give both fractions the same bottom number, 35. 4/5 is the same as 28/35, and 4/7 is the same as 20/35. 28/35 is more than 20/35, so 4/5 is bigger. 4/7 has the bigger bottom number, but that cuts the whole into smaller parts.

Perimeter is the distance all the way round the rectangle. One long and one short side make 9 plus 5, which is 14 cm. There are two of each, so double 14 cm to get 28 cm. 45 cm is 9 times 5, which finds the area instead. 23 cm leaves out one 5 cm side.
Count on from 7:50 pm to 9:20 pm. 7:50 pm to 8:50 pm is 1 hour. 8:50 pm to 9:20 pm is 30 minutes more. So the film lasts 1 h 30 min. 1 h 70 min treats an hour as 100 minutes.

First find the cost of the apples: 4 times 65p is £2.60. Add the juice: £2.60 plus £2.30 is £4.90. Take £4.90 from £10 to find the change. £4.90 plus 10p makes £5, and £5 more makes £10, so £5.10. £4.90 is the cost of the shopping, not the change.

Give each decimal three places: 0.600, 0.550, 0.400 and 0.049. Now compare them as thousandths: 600, 550, 400 and 49. 600 is the largest, so 0.6 is the largest decimal. 0.55 looks bigger because 55 is more than 6, but 0.550 is less than 0.600. 0.049 has the most digits, but its tenths digit is 0.
Find the pasta for one person first. 240 g shared by 3 is 80 g each. Five people need 80 g times 5, which is 400 g. 242 g just adds 2 g for the 2 extra people.

Line up 356 and 287 and add from the ones. 6 plus 7 is 13, so write 3 and carry 1. 5 plus 8 plus 1 is 14, so write 4 and carry 1. 3 plus 2 plus 1 is 6, giving 643. 543 leaves out the last carry, and 69 takes away instead of adding.

Write 483 above 176, lining up hundreds, tens and ones. In the ones, 3 is smaller than 6, so exchange a ten. 13 minus 6 is 7, and the tens now hold 7. 7 minus 7 is 0, and 4 minus 1 is 3, giving 307. 313 takes 3 from 6 in the ones instead of exchanging.

Find the money taken first: 320 tickets at £15 each. 320 times 10 is 3,200, and 320 times 5 is 1,600. Together that makes £4800. Take off the £1,200 costs to leave £3600 profit. £4800 is the money taken before the costs come off.

25% means 25 out of 100, which is one quarter. A quarter of £44 is £44 divided by 4. 44 divided by 4 is 11, so the answer is £11. £22 is half of £44, and £19 takes 25 off 44. £1,100 is 44 times 25, without dividing by 100.

Write £8 as £8.00 so the pounds and pence line up with £5.60. Take £5 from £8.00 to leave £3.00. Then take the 60p to leave £2.40. So Ben gets £2.40 change. £13.60 adds the prices instead of taking away.
